scope: Future matrix/grid contract sketch and current-core fit with graph/tree boundaries; no implementation or publication

conclusion.boundedTo: Finite dense rectangular generic matrices with fixed dimensions per trace, immutable values/marks/results, aggregate or per-cell scene strategies
conclusion.graphBoundary: Adjacency and conversions explicit; changing walls does not silently permit dynamic topology in the graph sketch
conclusion.treeBoundary: Predecessor maps require an explicit connected rooted subset and invariant checks before tree interpretation

requirements.coordinates: Zero-based row,column; safe fixed dimensions, exact dense row-major storage, valid zero-area shapes; practical size/storage limits require module API design
requirements.identity: Cells are model/address locations; moving entities have separate IDs; scene namespaces distinguish models, views, cells, graph and tree
requirements.lookup: scene.get only sees declared objects; aggregate cell lookup is via endpoint grid data and coordinates
requirements.ownership: Copied/frozen module-owned arrays and metadata; application T immutable/cloneable by caller; retained storage must not mutate or transfer-detach; no shared-memory exception
requirements.validation: Future module validates shape, bounds, references and updates atomically; generic Scene does not
requirements.animation: Generic core preserves endpoints/progress; renderer chooses discrete/numeric/crossfade policies, not implicit interpolation of T
requirements.performance: One scene object does not imply constant draw/copy cost; Player cannot interrupt one expensive source/render callback
requirements.moduleBoundary: Headless model; optional renderer and exact entry/import/graph/tree adapter boundaries remain undecided

runtimeProbe.scope: Current core with handwritten application grid states/scenes and existing examples; no new module implementation

checks.name: A dense grid is one generic Scene object
Aggregate transition retains both complete immutable endpoints
Values retain undefined, zero, false and empty-string payloads
Matrix update leaves earlier snapshot unchanged
Generic core preserves grid event, index and progress
Per-cell projection retains coordinate identities when contents swap
Row-column coordinates distinguish cells independently of equal values
Structured IDs separate cells, namespaces and projection modes
Aggregate scene.get does not invent virtual cell objects
Per-cell scene.get resolves the declared cell transition
Moving entity identity is independent of its cell
Cell overlays can share progress with moving entities
Immutable view filtering uses existing exit and presence
Exiting cell data remains available for an overlay
Restoring a filtered view uses existing enter transitions
Zero-area shapes remain distinct data without fake cells
Grid, graph and tree kinds compose in the current registry
Pure grid projection reuses endpoints without requiring an event
Aggregate handler receives values from both endpoints and raw progress
Grid state uses the current emitter without new fields
Terminal seek and hold preserve ordered result paths
Reverse frames preserve old and new grid data
Grid terminal closes once without extra reads
Fresh source restores cell contents and clears result
Buffered rewind restores prior grid without recomputation
State-only completion retains result with undefined event
Grid shape validation belongs to its module, not generic Scene
Changing projection kind under retained ID is still rejected
Existing maze uses an aggregate object with persistent path data
No-path remains algorithm state rather than a Player phase
Existing sand combines one field with stable grain identities
Plain grid state is structured-cloneable

typeProbe.scope: Application-only matrix/grid types against existing core/widget; no package declarations added
